FIRST ONSET SEIZURES 
 
History 
•
Detailed history of seizure 
•
NB! Recent history of head trauma? 
•
Drug use/abuse/overdose? 
 
Physical Examination 
•
Vital signs 
•
General examination & any evidence of underlying 
diseases, including trauma 
•
Neurological examination 
§
Signs of meningitis. NB Crypto can be subtle 
§
Focal neurological deficit 
Investigations 
•
ECG and blood glucose on ALL patients 
•
Tailor further investigations to clinical findings 
•
Urgent CT brain with contrast if 
§
No return to baseline  
§
Focal neurological deficit 
§
Features of raised ICP 
Discharge if: 
* Return to baseline  
* No significant concerns on clinical examination 
 
Note 
* DO NOT require anti-epileptic treatment 
* Follow up at Neuro OPD for workup  
Immediate Management 
•
ABCD approach to initial resuscitation 
•
Don’t ever forget glucose  
•
Hypoglycaemia: 1ml/kg of 50% Dextrose IV 
 
Airway and Breathing 
•
Patient position – lateral 
•
Supplemental oxygen (nasal prongs/FMO2) 
•
Rapid Sequence Intubation (RSI) if seizures continue for       
> 5 minutes (see RSI protocol) 
•
See Status Epilepticus protocol for further care 
 
Circulation 
•
Insert an IV line 
•
Shock:  Fluid bolus 20ml/kg of Balsol/Ringers Lactate 
 
Drugs 
•
Glucose if hypoglycaemia 
•
Benzodiazepine to abort seizure 
Admission Criteria 
•
Comorbidities e.g. renal failure, 
malnutrition 
•
Age > 60 years 
•
Immunocompromise 
•
Known cardiovascular disease 
•
Malignancy 
•
Pregnancy 
•
Focal neurology/delirium 
•
Toxins 
•
Trauma 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
